title: Quasi-holonomy in non-adiabatic quantum evolution
abstract: We develop a framework for quasi-holonomy in non-adiabatic quantum time evolution of subspaces along loops in a complex Grassmannian. By factoring the Schrödinger evolution into dynamical and connection-induced contributions in a moving basis, we obtain an effective geometric generator that depends explicitly on the dynamical propagator. This quasi-connection does not define a genuine connection on the original Grassmann bundle, since its gauge transformation law acquires a history-dependent, nonlocal term. Other ways of factoring the Schrödinger evolution are briefly discussed. All these approaches suffer from the same type of history-dependence, thereby defining transport of subspaces in which geometric and dynamical effects are generally intertwined, just as in the case of the quasi-holonomy. Our work sheds light on the issue of separating quantum evolution of subspaces into holonomic and dynamical parts from an essentially gauge-theoretic perspective.
summary: The paper develops a framework to analyze the separation of quantum subspace evolution into geometric (holonomic) and dynamical parts. By examining the quasi-connection derived from factoring the Schrödinger equation on the Grassmannian, the authors prove that this connection is not truly geometric due to history-dependent gauge transformations. This shows that in non-adiabatic regimes, quantum geometry and dynamics remain fundamentally intertwined.
main_problem: The paper investigates how to separate the quantum time evolution of subspaces into purely geometric (holonomic) and dynamical components when evolving along loops in a complex Grassmannian.
main_result: The quasi-connection derived from factoring the Schrödinger evolution does not define a genuine connection because its gauge transformation acquires an unavoidable, history-dependent term, implying that geometric and dynamical effects are generally inseparable.
method: The authors develop a framework by factoring the Schrödinger evolution into contributions associated with a dynamical propagator $D(t)$ and a quasi-connection $	ext{AD}(t)$, analyzing the resulting gauge transformation properties.
model_or_system: The system models the time evolution of $M$-dimensional subspaces within an $N$-dimensional Hilbert space, mathematically described by paths on the complex Grassmannian $G(N; M)$ and governed by a matrix differential equation derived from the Schrödinger equation.
key_observables: The quasi-connection $	ext{AD}(t) \equiv D^\dagger(t)	ext{A}(t)D(t)$, and its comparison to the transformation law of a true connection.
important_parameters: Cyclic evolution ($\Omega(	au) = \mathrm{IM}$), non-adiabatic regime, and the structure of the Hamiltonian generators $K(t)$ and $A(t)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to cyclic evolution; the core limitation is that separation fails due to gauge-theoretic obstructions.
figures_summary: Not specified by the notes provided, but the structure revolves around comparing different factorizations of the propagator $W(	au)$ (Eqs. 11, 25, 32) and analyzing their transformation properties.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general evolution equation for subspaces, proposes factoring it using a dynamical propagator to define a quasi-connection ($	ext{AD}(t)$), rigorously proves that this quasi-connection fails the criteria of a true connection due to history dependence, and concludes that separation is generally impossible.
why_interesting: This work provides deep theoretical insight into geometric phases in open or non-adiabatic quantum systems by formalizing when and why simple factorization methods fail, which has implications for understanding decoherence and adiabatic passage protocols.
